about: Stages and timing for the lifecycle-gap playbook. scripts/handoff.py reads this file: the stages it tracks, the outcomes each stage can record, and how long to wait between stages. Each key is explained under notes.

stages.name: find
stages.do: Map which lifecycle flows the project runs, add the missing, weak, draft and stopped ones as findings, and ask the user which gap to fill.

stages.name: launch
stages.do: Clone a proven scenario for the chosen flow as a draft after its own yes, or find there is nothing to clone or that a draft already exists.

skip_when.reason: the find stage found no lifecycle flow missing or weak.

stages.name: adapt
stages.do: Build the flow from the outline when there was nothing to clone, or make the launch fix list's step changes in the draft, each after its own yes.

skip_when.reason: the find stage found no lifecycle flow missing or weak.
the user stopped before any flow was made.

stages.name: qa
stages.do: QA the draft until it is GO; a NO-GO fix goes back through the adapt stage's write skill (engagement-scenario-builder), with its own yes, and is QA'd again. Then wait for the user to switch it on in the Engagement UI, record the day it started, and record the switch-on as a change (source engagement-ui).

skip_when.reason: the find stage found no lifecycle flow missing or weak.
the user stopped before any flow was made.

stages.name: health
stages.do: Check the new flow is sending: not suppressed, not failing, not stuck behind a condition nobody passes.

skip_when.reason: the find stage found no lifecycle flow missing or weak.
the user stopped before any flow was made.
the flow was never switched on.

stages.name: performance
stages.do: Read the flow's results step by step since it started: sends, clicks, unsubscribes and recipients who bought soon after.

skip_when.reason: the find stage found no lifecycle flow missing or weak.
the user stopped before any flow was made.
the flow was never switched on.

stages.name: impact
stages.do: Measure the business outcome the flow targets before and after it started, against a control, for a revenue verdict with a range.

skip_when.reason: the find stage found no lifecycle flow missing or weak.
the user stopped before any flow was made.
the flow was never switched on.

notes.health_check_days: Days after the qa stage finishes (the day the user switched the flow on) before the health stage is due. engagement-journey-health compares two 14-day halves; a flow younger than that can look quiet for good reasons.
notes.measure_after_days: Days after the flow started before the performance and impact stages are due. engagement-scenario-performance reads the last 30 days by default, and change-impact-tracker needs about 14 days after a change for a verdict other than too early to tell; 30 gives both a full month of a flow that fires on behaviour.
notes.wait_outcomes: Outcomes that mean a stage isn't finished yet. The script records them only with status in_progress and a --not-before date to come back on, so status never shows the stage as due before then.
notes.playbooks: Each playbook's title, product and stages in order. A stage names the skill that does it, whether that skill writes, what to do, the outcomes it can record, not_before (wait this rules key's number of days after another stage is done) and skip_when (suggest skipping when another stage had one of these outcomes; skips don't cascade, so each stage lists every earlier outcome that ends the run). The adapt stage is not in the original proposal: scenario-template-launcher never edits the clone and hands step changes, and flows with nothing to clone, to engagement-scenario-builder. The impact stage is added because engagement-scenario-performance counts buyers, not revenue; change-impact-tracker measures before and after, as there is no Engagement A/B setup skill.
